messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: elevated p95 latency on runtime-canary (us-west-2) — 10m p95 = 1.8s, baseline 200ms. Rate up ~2x. Paging eng-oncall.

maria: saw it, joining. grabbing traces now.

raj: noticed a spike in kernel-fallbacks on the canary pool at 1738499800-ish. batching queue exploded. metrics: kernel_fallback_rate 18% -> 65%.

maria: thanks. are canary nodes on the new attention-kernel patch?

raj: yes — rolled kernel v2 to canary 20m ago with adaptive-batching enabled. I think fallback is causing sawtooth latency.

maria: copying logs:```
[2024-11-02T12:00:12Z] warn: kernel_selector: no optimized kernels for seq_len=2048, falling back to reference.
[2024-11-02T12:00:12Z] info: batcher_queue.size=1240, avg_hold_ms=1200
[2024-11-02T12:00:13Z] error: prefetch_eviction=high
```

jess: oncall, taking handoff in 2m. maria please list mitigation options.

maria: options: 1) flip feature flag to route canary traffic to kernel v1 (kill-switch) 2) throttle canary qps at the loadbalancer 3) rollback canary rollout entirely. quickest = 1.

lucas: CS here — any ETA to stabilize? customers on trial experiencing text-gen timeouts. need a callback to affected accounts list.

raj: I can flip kill-switch. command:```sh
featureflagctl set runtime_kernel_v2 false --scope=canary --who=maria
```

maria: go for it. raj, say when you run it so I can notify support.

raj: running now...

incident-bot: ACTION: feature flag change detected by audit — runtime_kernel_v2=false (actor=raj) at 1738501292.

maria: observed immediate drop in kernel_fallback_rate to 7% within 30s. batcher_queue down to 220. p95 trending toward 300ms. :tada:

lucas: notifying affected customers now. sending note: "We've detected elevated latency; mitigation in progress; no data loss; follow-up scheduled."

jess: thanks team. I will keep monitoring and will coordinate rollback if we see residual regressions. handing off to eng-oncall for the night — jess oncall.

maria: quick postmortem notes: root cause looks like an optimizer-kernel mismatch under long sequences causing inefficient codepath + batching policy that aggressively aggregated long seqs. follow-ups: tighten selector, add seq_len gating in batcher, add green/amber flag for kernel flip during rollout.

jess: creating incident ticket and assigning to eng-runtime/raj for kernel fix, eng-batcher/maria for batching policy, and product for rollout checklist. closing page. last checked 1738501380 — metrics stable.
